item.text: {"summary":"An annual to biennial mustard native to Eurasia, Brassica rapa includes cultivated forms such as turnips, bok choy and napa cabbage. Wild and weedy forms typically have a slender taproot and leafy rosette, while turnip forms develop a swollen storage root; most flowers have four yellow petals followed by narrow seed pods. Cultivated varieties are eaten as roots or leafy vegetables, with young leaves eaten raw and older leaves typically cooked.","humanEdibility":"yes","edibilityNote":"Cultivated roots and leafy vegetables are eaten; young leaves may be raw, older leaves are typically cooked, and raw seeds may irritate some people.","evidence":{"summary":["s1:p2","s1:p3","s1:p11","s1:p15"],"humanEdibility":["s1:p15"]}}
